summary: Pre-market 2026-11-02: the composite risk score is 62.70 in the high_risk band and the model still reads risk_on, down only 0.23 from the settled 2026-10-30 row. Friday's US close was a one-way de-rating of semiconductors and AI hardware: the semiconductor theme fell 8.2415%, the four-name semiconductor leaders basket 6.4715%, AMD 10.8789% and SPY 1.7729%, while consumer staples and duration both caught a bid, which reads as valuation compression rather than a credit event. Monday's Asian session repaired part of it: 9 of the 11 tracked A-shares rose, averaging 1.4932%. The damage that matters is breadth: the share of names above their 200-day average is down to 0.3613, with 34 new lows against only 2 new highs. Two things to watch today: whether Apple's post-close report holds the AI narrative, and whether Friday's semiconductor selling carries into the US open.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation sits at 75.00 and is the single largest contributor at 11.25 points: 6 of the 8 production-scored signals are triggering. The set spans equities, the dollar, real rates, small-cap relative strength and bitcoin, which reads as multi-point confirmation rather than one noisy leg dragging the dimension.

High-yield OAS widened from 3.14 to 3.26, the 78.5 percentile of its own history, contributing 6.28 points, while investment-grade OAS moved only from 0.86 to 0.89 over the same span. Credit is widening, but at a pricing level rather than funding stress.

The 10-year yield sits at 4.98%, below the prior 5.05%, and the 10-year real rate at 2.63% in the 97.83 percentile, contributing 4.89 points. The long end eased modestly, but the real rate remains in an extreme band and keeps discounting long-duration growth.

Breadth is the clearest deterioration of the week: only 56 of 155 names hold their 200-day average, a 0.3613 share, and out of 157 there are 34 new lows against 2 new highs, contributing 4.80 points. The index-level loss is far smaller than the internal damage.

AI hardware is de-rating systematically: the semiconductor theme fell 8.2415%, AI infrastructure 7.8903% and networking 7.6692%, with all 19 US-only theme rows lower and a mean decline of 4.4111%. The only two positive rows in the table (memory 2.7930, consumer electronics 4.1791) are Asian-session reads: the memory row collapses to its two Korean constituents in the final step, so it does not signal US memory strength, with Micron down 5.3015% on the day.

supporting_signals.claim: The new-high ratio is only 0.0127: 2 new highs out of 157 against 34 new lows. Upside momentum is concentrated in very few names, so any index-level drawdown gets amplified by the internal structure.

Over a 63-trading-day window, semiconductors lag by 6.8672 percentage points and small caps by 5.4445 points. Both windows say the same thing: the leadership base is shrinking, not merely rotating for a day.

The index itself is still 3.686% above its 200-day average and only 2.9997% off its 52-week high, so the drawdown is happening inside the market rather than at the index level. The gap between index resilience and internal damage is the most fragile link right now.

contradicting_signals.claim: Volatility is not confirming the selloff: VIX settled at 17.20, the 46.43 percentile, and realized volatility is only 11.59, even though semiconductors are down 18.1875% on the month. The options market is not pricing systemic risk at all.

Credit is not deteriorating in step: investment-grade OAS moved only from 0.86 to 0.89, and high-yield at 3.26 stays well below the 4.00 warning threshold. A growth shock would not widen spreads by just 12 basis points.

A-shares did not follow: 9 of the 11 tracked names rose, averaging 1.4932%, with 688008.SH up 3.9672% and 603986.SH up 3.0528%. The Asian session treated Friday's US semiconductor selling as an external event.
The selling is concentrated in the AI compute chain: autos fell only 0.8653%, TSLA 0.8654% and fintech 0.0447%. Capital is migrating inside equities, not leaving them.

what_changed_today: The score reads 62.70, which is 3.37 above the 59.33 of the last pre-market brief, but 3.60 of that is the post-close restatement of 2026-10-30; the genuine overnight change is a 0.23 decline.
Breadth was rewritten by Friday's close: the share above the 200-day average fell from 0.4516 to 0.3613, new lows rose from 20 to 34 and new highs fell from 5 to 2.

The only meaningful dimension move is equity structure, from 70.62 to 69.51, with the new-lows sub-score easing from 45.94 to 39.58; the other five dimensions are essentially unchanged, so the total fell just 0.23.

Rate and credit vintages advanced to 2026-10-29: the 10-year from 5.05% to 4.98%, the real rate from 2.67% to 2.63%, high-yield OAS from 3.14 to 3.26 and VIX from 16.91 to 17.20. Friday's duration move is not in the score yet.
A-shares flipped from the prior session's broad decline to 9 names higher and a 1.4932% mean gain, the first directional reversal of the week.
watch_next: Apple reports after today's close and AMD follows tomorrow; together they decide whether Friday's semiconductor de-rating extends or mean-reverts.
The US midterm election is on 2026-11-03, and expectations for congressional control can move sector rotation ahead of fundamentals.
This week's macro data clusters late: JOLTS on 2026-11-03, the Employment Situation on 2026-11-06 and CPI on 2026-11-10 are the three gates for the rate path.

The rate and credit inputs in the score stop at 2026-10-29 and the FX block is still the stale 2026-10-23 vintage. If the long end keeps rallying, the score gets revised lower on the next refresh, not today.

Hormuz tanker risk is still live: Iran claims 11 tankers have caught fire since 2026-10-25, while US-Iran contacts have pushed crude back below 100 dollars. If the talks fail, the inflation side reverses immediately.
There is incremental domestic policy support: the PBoC launches a third SFISF operation on 2026-11-03 with a wider participant base, and broad-based ETFs have seen 20 consecutive sessions of inflows.

bull_case.title: Bull case: volatility and credit keep denying the selloff
points: VIX at 17.20 and realized volatility at 11.59 say the options market is not pricing systemic risk; if Friday was position clearing, the index repairs quickly.
High-yield OAS at 3.26 stays below the 4.00 threshold and investment grade at 0.89 has barely moved, so financing conditions have not tightened.
A-shares and Korean memory rebounded together, with 9 of 11 tracked names up and a 1.4932% mean gain, which says Asian demand has not deteriorated in step.

base_case.title: Base case: sideways digestion inside the high_risk band
points: The score oscillates around 62.70 and the daily move is just 0.23, which says the model has entered a plateau.
Breadth stalls at 0.3613 with 34 new lows while AI hardware grinds lower and staples plus duration absorb the flow, keeping index losses contained.
Cross-asset confirmation holds at 6 of 8, and its 75.00 contribution caps how fast the score can break higher.

bear_case.title: Bear case: Apple and AMD falsify the AI capex story
points: If Apple's post-close report or AMD's guidance disappoints, the 6.8672 percentage-point semiconductor underperformance extends and equity structure at 69.51 keeps climbing at a 20% weight.
Cross-asset confirmation still has 2 legs untriggered, and filling them would visibly enlarge that dimension's contribution and step the total up.

If breadth slides further from 0.3613 and new lows exceed 34, the model reads that as trend deterioration rather than noise; a breakdown in the Hormuz talks would also lift crude and reignite the inflation side of a 72.37 macro dimension.
